cross_validation.method: leanexpr.py vs extract/api.py over every evaluated argument tuple

contract_totality.method: strict-arithmetic leanexpr vs lean_rt-backed extract, same points

simpleFst-is-nei.claim: simpleFst p1 p2 equals Nei's G_ST for two equally weighted demes
simpleFst-is-nei.model_definition: biallelic, two demes, parametric allele frequencies
simpleFst-is-nei.canfail_clause: grid must include |p1-p2| large AND pbar far from 0.5: at p1=p2 both sides are 0 and at pbar=0.5 the Nei and Hudson denominators coincide, so a symmetric grid cannot separate the conventions

simpleFst-vs-hudson.claim: CONVENTION PIN: is simpleFst Hudson's F_ST rather than Nei's?
simpleFst-vs-hudson.canfail_clause: needs pbar != 0.5; Nei and Hudson coincide exactly at pbar=0.5
simpleFst-vs-hudson.note: expected to DISAGREE; that disagreement is the pin

unmodelled_hypotheses: meanAlleleFreq p₁ p₂ * (1 - meanAlleleFreq p₁ p₂

neiFst-identity.claim: neiFst H_T H_S fed the two-deme heterozygosities reproduces G_ST
neiFst-identity.model_definition: H_T, H_S supplied by the caller
neiFst-identity.model_reference: H_S = mean within-deme het, H_T = het of pooled frequency
neiFst-identity.canfail_clause: p1 != p2 required; at p1=p2, H_T=H_S and both sides are 0

hudson-sample-limit.claim: SELF-TEST of the reference: Hudson's finite-n estimator -> parametric
hudson-sample-limit.canfail_clause: see hudson-sample-small-n: the same comparison at n=20 fails
hudson-sample-limit.note: guards the reference itself, not the corpus; the corpus mutants do not touch it, so its power is demonstrated by the companion check hudson-sample-small-n rather than by mutation

hudson-sample-small-n.claim: DEMONSTRATION that the previous check has power: at n=20 it fails
hudson-sample-small-n.canfail_clause: self-evident: this check exists to fail
hudson-sample-small-n.note: expected to DISAGREE; this is the can-fail evidence for hudson-sample-limit

coalFst-exact-split.claim: coalFst t Ne is exactly Hudson F_ST after a clean split
coalFst-exact-split.model_definition: split t generations ago; one size parameter Ne
coalFst-exact-split.model_reference: clean split, N_daughter = N_ancestral = Ne, infinite sites
coalFst-exact-split.canfail_clause: t must reach order Ne. For t << Ne every candidate F_ST formula collapses to t/(2Ne) and the check cannot discriminate.

coalFst-asymmetric-sizes.claim: SCOPE: coalFst has one Ne, so it cannot express unequal daughter sizes
coalFst-asymmetric-sizes.model_definition: single Ne; caller must pick one
coalFst-asymmetric-sizes.canfail_clause: THE asymmetry: N1 != N2. With N1 = N2 the check reduces to coalFst-exact-split and passes trivially.
coalFst-asymmetric-sizes.note: expected to disagree; quantifies the cost of the single-size assumption

fstDerived-is-not-split-fst.claim: MODEL: the drift recurrence is not the F_ST of a split
fstDerived-is-not-split-fst.model_reference: clean split at mutation-drift equilibrium, infinite sites
fstDerived-is-not-split-fst.canfail_clause: REQUIRES t/(2Ne) >= ~0.5. Both sides are t/(2Ne) + O(t^2/Ne^2), so at t << Ne they agree to <1% and the test is vacuous.

fstDerived-is-coalescence-prob.claim: what fstDerived actually computes: P(coalesce within t) in a closed pop
fstDerived-is-coalescence-prob.canfail_clause: t >= 1 and Ne finite; at t=0 both sides are 0

hetLossFromDrift-duplicates-fstDerived.claim: DUPLICATE: identical body to fstDerived under a different name
hetLossFromDrift-duplicates-fstDerived.canfail_clause: t >= 1; at t=0 both sides are 0

fstFromGenerations-equals-coalFst.claim: cross-file: fstFromGenerations agrees with the exact split F_ST

pairwiseFstFromBranches.claim: multiplicative branch composition vs the exact two-branch split F_ST
pairwiseFstFromBranches.model_reference: clean split, both daughters size Ne, total separation tS+tT
pairwiseFstFromBranches.canfail_clause: needs tS+tT of order Ne AND ideally tS != tT. At tS,tT << Ne the composition is exact to first order.

hetEquilibrium-vs-exact-iam.claim: theta/(1+theta) vs the exact infinite-alleles stationary heterozygosity
hetEquilibrium-vs-exact-iam.canfail_clause: needs mu large enough that (1-mu)^2 != 1-2mu; mu >= 1e-3
hetEquilibrium-vs-exact-iam.note: agreement to O(mu) is the claim; tol reflects that

hetDecayFactor-vs-exact-eigenvalue.model_definition: theta passed in must be 4*Ne*mu for the SAME Ne

hetMutationDriftRecurrence-trajectory.claim: the corpus recurrence vs the exact IAM trajectory from H0=0
hetMutationDriftRecurrence-trajectory.canfail_clause: H0 must differ from H*, and t must not be so large that both sides have converged to H* -- at t -> inf the trajectory check degenerates into the equilibrium check and cannot see a wrong eigenvalue.

transient-discrete-vs-continuous.claim: discrete and continuous transients agree only for large Ne
transient-discrete-vs-continuous.canfail_clause: Ne must go down to ~5; at Ne=5000 the two agree to 1e-4
transient-discrete-vs-continuous.note: internal consistency; reference is another corpus definition

islandModelFst-finite-demes.canfail_clause: d must include small values. At d=40 the correction is 5% and at d -> inf it vanishes, so a large-d-only grid cannot fail.

fstIslandMultiplicative-exact-fixedpoint.canfail_clause: m must reach ~0.3 so the (1-m)^2 terms matter

islandModelFst-vs-exact-in-m.claim: 1/(1+4Nm) vs the exact-in-m island fixed point
islandModelFst-vs-exact-in-m.canfail_clause: m >= 0.1; at m <= 1e-3 the expansion is exact to 0.1%

steppingStoneLength-missing-mutation.model_definition: L = sqrt(2 Ne m); no mutation argument
steppingStoneLength-missing-mutation.canfail_clause: the grid MUST vary mu at fixed Ne and m: the Lean value is constant along that axis while the reference moves as mu^-1/2. Varying only Ne and m would let a fitted constant hide the error.

steppingStone-cross-file-contradiction.canfail_clause: d must be comparable to or larger than L; at d -> 0 both -> 0

demoSteppingStoneFst-exact.claim: d/(d+4 Ne m sigma^2) is the Hudson F_ST built from its own T(d)
demoSteppingStoneFst-exact.canfail_clause: d > 0 and finite Ne; at d=0 both sides are 0

ldRetentionPerGen-exact.claim: (1-r)(1-1/2Ne) is the exact per-generation retention of E[D]
ldRetentionPerGen-exact.model_definition: two neutral loci, recombination r, Wright-Fisher Ne
ldRetentionPerGen-exact.canfail_clause: r > 0 and Ne finite; at r=0, Ne=inf both sides are 1

ldHalfLife-drops-recombination.claim: FORMULA: 2 Ne ln2 is the r=0 half-life; the true one depends on r
ldHalfLife-drops-recombination.model_definition: half-life = 2 Ne ln 2; no recombination argument
ldHalfLife-drops-recombination.model_reference: ln2 / -ln[(1-r)(1-1/2Ne)], from ldRetentionPerGen in the same file
ldHalfLife-drops-recombination.canfail_clause: REQUIRES r >> 1/(2Ne). At r=0 the two are identical, and that is exactly the degenerate point a careless grid would sit on.

ldRetainedFraction-inconsistent-with-ret.claim: INTERNAL: retained fraction is not ldRetentionPerGen^t
ldRetainedFraction-inconsistent-with-ret.canfail_clause: r > 0 required; the r=0 row is in the grid and passes, which is the point

driftLDEquilibrium-exact-fixedpoint.claim: closed form is the exact fixed point of driftLDStep
driftLDEquilibrium-exact-fixedpoint.canfail_clause: c up to 0.3 so the (1-c)^2 factor is not ~1

driftLDEquilibrium-vs-ohta-kimura.claim: MODEL: the IBD equilibrium is not Ohta-Kimura's sigma_d^2 = E[r^2]
driftLDEquilibrium-vs-ohta-kimura.model_definition: probability of gametic identity by descent (Sved)
driftLDEquilibrium-vs-ohta-kimura.canfail_clause: REQUIRES rho = 4Nc <~ 10. The two forms converge as rho -> inf (2% apart at rho=100), so a tightly-linked-only grid is essential.

driftLDTrajectory-converges.claim: iterating driftLDStep from Q0=0 reaches driftLDEquilibrium
driftLDTrajectory-converges.canfail_clause: Q0 must differ from the equilibrium; Q0=0 is chosen for that reason

selectionMigrationEquilibrium.claim: closed form vs the exact fixed point of its own one-generation map
selectionMigrationEquilibrium.canfail_clause: grid must straddle m = s. Below it the polymorphism is protected and any formula of the right shape looks fine; at and above m = s the allele is lost and a wrong formula returns a positive frequency.

alleleFreqAfterMigration.claim: p_c + (p0-p_c)(1-m)^t is the exact solution of the migration recursion
alleleFreqAfterMigration.canfail_clause: p0 != p_c required; otherwise the frequency never moves

admixedFst-ratio-not-numerator.claim: (1-alpha)^2 scaling ignores that F_ST is a ratio, not a numerator
admixedFst-ratio-not-numerator.canfail_clause: REQUIRES pbar to move with alpha, i.e. p_a and p_b far apart and both away from 0.5. If p_a + p_b = 1 the denominators coincide and the (1-alpha)^2 numerator scaling is exactly right -- a symmetric frequency pair makes this check unable to fail.

dup-islandModelFst-fstMigDriftEquil.canfail_clause: arguments differ between rows; identical bodies give 0 error by construction

pairwiseFstFromBranchTaus-correct-compos.claim: the tau-additive composition IS the exact two-branch split F_ST
pairwiseFstFromBranchTaus-correct-compos.model_reference: clean split, total separation tS+tT, equal sizes
pairwiseFstFromBranchTaus-correct-compos.canfail_clause: tS+tT of order Ne, and tS != tT rows included so an incorrect symmetric-only composition cannot hide.
pairwiseFstFromBranchTaus-correct-compos.note: PortabilityDrift contains both compositions; this one is exact and pairwiseFstFromBranches is not. They are not alternatives.

expectedHeterozygosity-equals-hetEquilib.claim: theta/(1+theta) composed with theta=4Ne mu reproduces hetEquilibrium
expectedHeterozygosity-equals-hetEquilib.canfail_clause: identity by construction; recorded as a duplicate, not a validation

ldCorrelationFromMigration-vs-sharedLD-s.claim: M^2/(1+M)^2 is exactly the square of PortabilityDrift.sharedLDFromMigration
ldCorrelationFromMigration-vs-sharedLD-s.model_definition: proportion of LD that is shared, as a function of M=4Nm
ldCorrelationFromMigration-vs-sharedLD-s.canfail_clause: M must be away from the fixed points of x->x^2 (0 and 1); M=1 gives 0.25 vs 0.5
ldCorrelationFromMigration-vs-sharedLD-s.note: CONSISTENT: PopulationGeneticsFoundations.ldCorrelationFromMigration is exactly the square of PortabilityDrift.sharedLDFromMigration, i.e. (1 - islandModelFst)^2. Both are 'shared LD' but one is a correlation and the other its square; the relation is exact and now recorded.

targetHetFromFst-tautology.claim: het_source*(1-fst) is exactly the rearrangement of fstFromHetRatio
targetHetFromFst-tautology.model_definition: F_ST defined as fractional heterozygosity loss
targetHetFromFst-tautology.canfail_clause: none available. The composition is the identity for every input, so no grid can make it fail -- which is the finding, not a defect of the check.
targetHetFromFst-tautology.note: confirms the corpus's own VACUOUS annotation: this round-trips to the identity and so carries no empirical content about F_ST

neutralAFBenchmarkRatio-bounded.claim: (1-fstT)/(1-fstS) vs the heterozygosity ratio it is meant to be
neutralAFBenchmarkRatio-bounded.model_definition: ratio of retained heterozygosity, drift-only closed population
neutralAFBenchmarkRatio-bounded.model_reference: exact IAM heterozygosity ratio between two branches at mutation-drift balance
neutralAFBenchmarkRatio-bounded.canfail_clause: tS != tT is mandatory. At tS = tT the definition returns exactly 1 and so does the reference -- the symmetric design in which both sides collapse to 1 is precisely the false-validation failure mode.
neutralAFBenchmarkRatio-bounded.note: the reference starts each branch AT equilibrium, so the true ratio is 1: mutation replenishes what drift removes. The definition predicts a ratio far from 1 because its model has no mutation.

wrightFIT-composition.canfail_clause: both f_IS and f_ST nonzero in at least one row; at f_IS=0 it reduces to f_ST
